sources.facts: The official museum traces the lodge and mausoleum to the original Seljuk rose garden.
The official survey names the west and north dervish cells, south kitchen and gates, and the east mausoleum, prayer room and semahane. It identifies the covered fountain and the pool.
The completed restoration records the 16 turquoise ribs and conical roof of Kubbe-i Hadra.
The authors measured 30.5 m square for the tomb core and 68 m by 84 m for the courtyard, with laser scanning and conventional survey.
Museum director Naci Bakırcı identifies the connected ritual hall and worship room, the latter’s south-west portico tower with one balcony, and the eighteen historical dervish cells.
The measured Kubbe-i Hadra height is 25 m in the restoration history.
The museum overview confirms the 25 m tomb height, a sixteen-rib cylinder and cone, small domes and chimneys above the dervish cells, and named court structures.
